concepts.name: Forced Prioritization
concepts.description: The practice of deliberately choosing the single most important message, objective, or idea when multiple valid options compete for attention.

concepts.name: Message Triage
concepts.description: The process of eliminating secondary messages so that communication remains focused on the highest-priority idea.

concepts.name: Decision Paralysis
concepts.description: A state where complexity, uncertainty, or competing options make it difficult to choose a course of action.

problems.name: Decision paralysis under uncertainty
problems.description: People struggle to make decisions when faced with uncertainty, complexity, or multiple competing possibilities.

problems.name: Message dilution
problems.description: A communication loses impact because too many important messages compete for attention at the same time.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Finding the core requires forced prioritization
insights.what_it_says: Communicators often lose sight of the core message because they become immersed in details and complexity. Finding the core requires choosing one central idea and resisting the temptation to communicate everything at once.
insights.why_it_matters: People cannot easily remember or act on multiple competing priorities. Clear communication depends on identifying and emphasizing the single most important message.

examples_from_source.what_happened: Journalists often become immersed in details and lose track of the most important element of a story, leading to buried leads.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: The example shows how expertise and information abundance can obscure what audiences actually need to know.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: When communicating, identify the one thing the audience must remember before adding supporting details.

decision_rules.condition: When multiple important ideas compete for attention.
decision_rules.action: Identify the single most important message and communicate it first.
decision_rules.rationale: A message with one clear priority is easier to understand and remember.

patterns.description: Reduce complexity by selecting one dominant idea.

warnings.warning: Do not allow details to overshadow the core message.
warnings.consequence: The audience may miss the most important point.
warnings.prevention: Continually evaluate whether each detail supports the central idea.

application_patterns.when_to_use: When explaining complex topics, strategies, products, or initiatives.
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Applicable to writing, presentations, marketing, leadership, and teaching.

when_not_to_use: When the objective is comprehensive reference documentation
tradeoffs: Simplicity may omit nuance, but improves clarity and memorability.
insights.evidence: There's only one lead, and there's only one core. You must choose.

relationships.evidence: Finding the core and writing the lead both involve forced prioritization.
There has to be message triage.
